clue.text: The growth of revolutionary Maoism

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters of the word Maoism are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark about how revolutionary Maoism spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like it goes with Maoism in a political sense, but it signals an anagram of MAOISM.
explanation.definitionFit: The mimosa is a plant, and any plant can be called a growth.

clue.text: Oil many a fool put in vehicle

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword shorthand for many

indicators.note: put in means the fool goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Lots of oil, and a fool stuck in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Macassar was a Victorian hair oil, hence the antimacassar on chair backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian men slicked their hair with this oil, named after a port in Indonesia.

clue.text: Gleeman's unusual medley

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the minstrel's name are arranged in a way out of the ordinary

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A minstrel performs an odd mixture of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: A gleeman is a medieval minstrel; his name is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mélange is a mixture, which is what a medley is.

clue.text: Underemphasise what produces piano music?

definitions.meaning: to play down or tone down
the pedal that quietens a piano; piano in music means soft

explanation.surface: Downplay whatever makes music at the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' in musical notation means quietly, so piano music here is soft music.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to tone it down, like the quietening pedal on the instrument.

clue.text: Two measures taken in part of March

parts.note: a foot is a measure of length
a step is also used as a rough measure of distance

explanation.surface: Two units of length are taken up in some section of the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M of March steers you to the month; it is a march as soldiers do it.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is made up of a soldier's paces, each one a single stride of the parade.

clue.text: Conversely, where one might reckon to be after five?

definitions.meaning: from the opposite point of view

definitions.text: where one might reckon to be after five?
definitions.meaning: counting on fingers, the sixth is on the second set of fingers

explanation.surface: On the contrary, where you might expect to be after five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reckon' means count: counting on fingers, after five you move to your other set of fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase introduces a contrasting point, meaning the reverse is also true.

clue.text: Wrong letters secretary finally put in post, perhaps

indicators.note: put in means the secretary's last letter goes inside the reworked word
perhaps means the word post could be arranged some other way
finally picks out the last letter of the word secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary sends off a letter full of mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges POST into TPOS; 'finally' takes Y from secretary, and 'put in' sets it inside: T-Y-POS.
explanation.definitionFit: Typing mistakes are wrongly struck characters in a text.

clue.text: There's a girl here, staring you in the face

indicators.note: staring you in the face says the name is right there in plain view in the clue's letters

explanation.surface: A woman stands right before you.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words, ignoring the apostrophe, spell out the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Red rag

parts.note: Red as in communist, rag as a slang term for a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: This was the official newspaper of the Soviet Communist Party, a communist paper.

clue.text: Get cross in game

parts.note: to contract an illness is to get it
to bridge a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: Someone becomes angry while playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get cross' reads as become angry; it is two verbs, catch and span.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the card game in which partnerships bid for the number of tricks.

clue.text: Unfriendly air displayed by weatherman

parts.note: an unfriendly manner is a cold one
an air or outward show put on is a front

explanation.surface: A forecaster presents a frosty manner on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather maps show the boundary where a mass of chilly air advances, and presenters point it out.

clue.text: Confused mass with odd bits of that religious work

parts.note: pie is a printers' word for a jumbled mass of type, hence any muddle

indicators.note: odd bits means the first and third letters of the word that, the odd-numbered positions

explanation.surface: A muddle mixed with stray parts of a sacred artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE in the printers' sense (spilt, jumbled type) is the 'Confused mass'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of Mary holding the dead Christ, a devotional artwork.

clue.text: Star's blemish given publicity in tabloid?

definitions.meaning: a dark patch seen on the face of our nearest star
a slot or feature in the Sun, a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A celebrity's skin flaw gets splashed across the gossip pages.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star suggests a celebrity, but it is the Sun in the sky; the Sun is also a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers call a cooler, darker patch on the solar surface by this name.

clue.text: Location for TV show, as opposed to live theatre

definitions.meaning: the area of London where the BBC soap ... is set
the opposite of London's West End, the district of live theatres

explanation.surface: Where a television programme is made, unlike a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running British TV soap opera; London's West End is its theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: The eastern part of London is both the soap's setting and the counterpart of the theatreland West End.

clue.text: Having more points each

definitions.meaning: per person, as in 'a pound a head'

explanation.surface: A contestant leads, point for point.
explanation.definitionFit: A team leading on points is in front; 'a head' means per person, so each.

clue.text: Holmes booked a table for this despot

definitions.text: Holmes booked a table for this
definitions.meaning: Oliver Wendell Holmes wrote the book The ... of the Breakfast-Table

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes reserves a restaurant table for a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes is not Sherlock but the American writer Oliver Wendell Holmes; 'booked a table' points to his book title, not a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot rules with unchecked power, as does an absolute ruler.

clue.text: Final letter penned by unorthodox educator in part of France

indicators.note: penned by means the letter is enclosed within the rearranged word
unorthodox means the letters of educator are arranged in a non-standard way

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A maverick teacher writes a last note from somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges EDUCATOR into COTEDAUR; 'penned by' puts Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Côte d'Azur is the French Riviera, a coastal region of the country.

clue.text: Reduce area of county

indicators.note: area of county puts the county's name before the word for area

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
size is extent or area

explanation.surface: Shrink the region of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland; 'of' makes it SIZE of DOWN, i.e. Down's size.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut back a business or other thing is to make it smaller.

clue.text: Put obstacle in the way of one form of gambling

indicators.note: Put ... in the way tells us the obstacle is placed inside the word for way

parts.note: a route is a way
a let is an obstacle, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Someone blocks the path to a kind of betting.
explanation.walkthrough: LET as an obstacle is old legal language: 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game played by betting on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Friendly way to address former head

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A warm greeting for a past headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former head' suggests an ex-headteacher; 'old bean' is a jovial, dated British form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: This chummy, old-fashioned British phrase greets a pal warmly.

clue.text: European poet's craft revealed in Chinese way

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': the European poet is the answer

indicators.note: revealed in places the craft inside the Chinese way

parts.note: Tao is the Way in Chinese philosophy
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: An Italian poet's skill shows in his Chinese manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft looks like skill, but it is a vessel, SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was an Italian Renaissance poet who wrote Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Pile on the cheese

parts.note: a pile is a post driven in for support, as is a stilt

explanation.surface: Load up the cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Stilton is a strong English blue cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a blue-veined English cheese.

clue.text: Money Jack raised kept in fortress

indicators.note: kept in means the sailor is held inside the word for money

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the sailor's letters are read upwards

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: Funds Jack collected are stored in a stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor (jack tar), AB; 'raised' reverses it to BA in this down entry, and 'kept in' places it in CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the citadel of a North African city.

clue.text: Book reviewer who appreciates a good reception?

definitions.meaning: someone who inspects a firm's books, its accounts
a listener, who likes clear radio reception

explanation.surface: A literary critic who enjoys a warm welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book reviewer' suggests a literary critic, but it is someone who checks account books.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant who examines financial records holds this title, and the Latin root means a hearer.

clue.text: Credit OK? You've capital invested there

indicators.note: invested means the city is wrapped up inside these words

explanation.surface: Is your credit good? You've put money into that capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' and 'invested' suggest finance; the city is tucked in creditOKYOu've.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: Hard-headed pope who created division here?

indicators.note: headed means the other piece is topped by the letter for hard

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Adrian was the name of several popes, including the English Adrian IV

explanation.surface: An obstinate pontiff who caused a schism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-headed' looks like stubborn, but splits into H heading the name of a pope. The Roman emperor built a wall across northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor ordered a wall built across Britain, splitting the province from the north.

clue.text: Crack to ruin potter's achievement

definitions.meaning: in snooker, a run of pots scored in one visit to the table

explanation.surface: A flaw that wrecks a craftsman's pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: The potter is not a ceramicist but a snooker player potting balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture, smashing something, and a snooker scoring sequence all share this one word.

clue.text: Put on Bizet, missing his first note — or another composer

parts.note: to don is to put on clothes

indicators.note: missing his first means the composer's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: the French composer of Carmen
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone stages Bizet but leaves out a note, or picks a different composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaetano Donizetti was an Italian opera composer, so he is a second composer besides Bizet.

clue.text: Present Duke in royal house

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for Duke inside the name of the royal house

parts.note: Hanover is the German royal house that ruled Britain from 1714 to 1901

explanation.surface: A gift for a duke at a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift noun but is the verb, to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to give it formally into someone's keeping.

clue.text: Medal for sculpture

definitions.meaning: a statue cast in that copper alloy

explanation.surface: An award given for a work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Third place earns a medal in this metal, and a cast statue is named after it too.
